labour_temp.title: Labour-market temperature
labour_temp.formula: Mean of five robust z-scores, each against its own trailing 10 years (median and 1.4826 x median absolute deviation, so 2020 does not swamp the scale), signed so positive means tighter: minus the 3-month change in the unemployment rate; minus initial claims' 4-week average against its own 52-week average (%); the 3-month average payroll change; the quits rate; job openings per unemployed person. Shown with the Sahm gap: 3-month average unemployment rate minus its lowest 3-month average of the prior 12 months.
labour_temp.limits: The October 2025 household-survey gap blanks 3-month averages that span it. The payroll pace that keeps unemployment steady is uncertain while immigration shifts labour supply, so payroll change is read against its own history, not a fixed neutral number. The Sahm gap's 0.5 pp line marked the start of every US recession since 1970 and triggered in August 2024 without one.
labour_temp.unit: average z-score (positive = tighter than its own 10-year median)

fed_reaction.title: Fed reaction: policy rate, rule and market path
fed_reaction.formula: Policy-range midpoint; the Atlanta Fed Taylor-rule utility's FOMCTaylor99UR prescription; the fed funds futures strip's implied rate for the next policy month and about 6 and 12 months out (100 minus price); the latest FOMC median projections. Value: the change the futures price over about 12 months (pp).
fed_reaction.limits: The neutral rate inside any Taylor rule is disputed; the utility shows one documented choice. Futures embed a term premium, so they are not a pure expectation.

fiscal_impulse.unit: pp of GDP (positive = fiscal policy putting more into demand than a year earlier)

side_rule.text: Each test sits WITH the view when its value is beyond the 'confirm' threshold, AGAINST it when beyond the 'refute' threshold, and NEITHER in between. With c tests with and r against: c - r >= 2 is 'with'; c - r = 1 is 'leaning with'; c = r (both above zero) is 'mixed'; no test past either threshold is 'neutral'; r - c = 1 is 'leaning against'; r - c >= 2 is 'against'. Fewer than half the tests with data is 'not enough data'.
